model.title: The Three Descents
model.premise: A gift under pressure does not switch off. It works harder in the wrong direction. What you see in a distressed person is not the absence of their gift — it is their gift aimed at the wrong target, usually at whoever is closest.
model.theology: Romans 12 names the gifts as grace given, not merit earned. Which means the descent is never evidence that the gift was false. It is evidence that the gift is being operated by fear instead of by faith. The way back is never to suppress the gift. It is to return it to its source.

stages.name: Strain
stages.description: The gift is still recognizable and still aimed at something real. It has simply lost its grace — it is louder, faster, and less patient than it should be. The person still believes they are serving. Others notice the edge and usually excuse it.
stages.reversal: Reversible in a single honest conversation. This is the cheapest place to intervene and the place almost everyone misses.

stages.name: Distortion
stages.description: The gift turns outward as a blade or a wall. It is now protecting the person rather than serving the room. Motives get assigned. People begin managing the distressed person instead of engaging them, which confirms every fear that put them here.
stages.reversal: Still reversible, but it now takes repair rather than clarification. Something was damaged and has to be named before it can be undone.

stages.name: Captivity
stages.description: The gift turns on its owner. The pattern is no longer something the person does; it is something that runs them. The strength has become the identity, and the identity has become a cell. From inside, captivity feels like clarity — which is exactly what makes it so hard to leave.
stages.reversal: Not self-correcting. This stage requires someone outside the pattern who is willing to stay. Insight alone will not lift it.

laws.title: The descent is always downhill from a real strength
laws.body: No one arrives at Captivity through a flaw. They arrive through a gift that was never given anywhere safe to land. Treat the pattern as a wounded strength, not as a character defect, or the person will defend it — correctly.

laws.title: Everyone descends in their own language
laws.body: Two people in identical distress will look nothing alike. One gets louder, one goes silent, one gets busy, one gets charming. Reading distress requires knowing the person's gift, not scanning for a universal set of warning signs.

laws.title: The flare is a request, badly worded
laws.body: Under every distress behavior is an unmet need the person has stopped being able to ask for directly. The behavior is the ask. Answer the need and the behavior loses its job.

laws.title: Pressure narrows the range
laws.body: In a good week, people operate across several gifts. Under pressure, everyone collapses back to their first gift and runs its flare. This is why relationships that work fine in ordinary conditions come apart in hard ones — the hard week is a different relationship.

catalyst.trigger: Being asked to pretend. The Catalyst descends when the truth in the room is obvious to them and unspeakable to everyone else, or when the words people say and the things they do stop matching and no one will name it.

descent.tell: Every observation acquires an edge.
descent.body: The Catalyst is still saying true things, but the truth has stopped being offered and started being delivered. Questions become tests. Praise gets a clause attached to it. They are not trying to wound anyone yet — they are trying to be heard, and volume is the only lever they can find.
descent.cost: People start pre-editing what they bring to this person, which removes exactly the raw information the Catalyst needs to do their work.

descent.tell: The problem stops being the system and becomes the people.
descent.body: Motives get assigned. What was a critique of a broken process becomes a verdict on someone's character, delivered with the certainty the Catalyst normally reserves for facts. They are now prosecuting rather than diagnosing, and they experience the pushback as further proof that everyone is compromised.
descent.cost: The Catalyst begins to be right about the wrong thing. The accuracy of the original insight gets buried under the injustice of the accusation, and no one can access the truth anymore.

descent.tell: Burning it down starts to feel like faithfulness.
descent.body: Nothing is redeemable. The Catalyst exits, detonates, or dismantles — the relationship, the role, the institution — and reads the wreckage as integrity. Cynicism has replaced discernment, and because cynicism is never technically wrong about anything, it is almost impossible to argue with from the inside.
descent.cost: The gift meant for renewal has done only demolition. The Catalyst is left isolated with an intact conviction and nothing built.

chronic.name: The Prosecutor
chronic.body: Every conversation becomes a case being made. The Catalyst is no longer looking for what is true; they are gathering evidence. Relationships become witnesses, and everyone learns to testify carefully.

catalyst.needs: Evidence that the truth actually landed somewhere. Not agreement — reception. And congruence: people whose actions match their words.
catalyst.sayThis: You're not wrong about this. Tell me what you see, and then tell me what you want done with it.
catalyst.notThisWhy: It confirms the Catalyst's deepest fear — that telling the truth costs them belonging. They will either escalate to be heard or leave to stop needing to be.
catalyst.ownMove: Separate the truth from the verdict. Name the problem out loud without assigning the motive behind it. The Catalyst's power is diagnostic, and a diagnosis stops working the moment it becomes an accusation.
catalyst.restoredBody: The willingness to say the hard thing for someone rather than at them — which is the only form of prophetic speech anyone can actually receive.

servant.trigger: Invisibility. The Servant descends when the work is real, the cost is real, and no one has noticed either — or when help that was freely offered starts being quietly expected.

descent.tell: The list grows and the request never comes.
descent.body: Rather than ask for help or name a limit, the Servant simply takes on more. They are still glad to do it, mostly. But the yes has started to be automatic rather than chosen, and somewhere underneath it a quiet arithmetic has begun.
descent.cost: Everyone around them recalibrates upward. The Servant's capacity becomes the new baseline expectation, and the very reliability that makes them valuable makes their limit invisible.

descent.tell: The help develops a bill attached to it.
descent.body: The scorekeeping surfaces — never as a direct statement, always as a sigh, a pointed aside, a martyred comment made half-joking. Service becomes leverage. The Servant would be horrified to hear it described this way, because from inside it feels like nothing more than wanting to be seen.
descent.cost: Gratitude becomes impossible to give. Anything offered now reads as payment on a debt, so even genuine thanks fails to satisfy, which proves to the Servant that no one really values them.

descent.tell: The breakdown, and the blame that follows it.
descent.body: The body or the will finally gives out, and the resentment that has been accumulating for years arrives all at once — aimed at the exact people the Servant spent themselves serving. Self-pity and bitterness braid together into a story in which they were used, and everyone else was the user.
descent.cost: The relationships the work was meant to build are the relationships the collapse destroys. Years of genuine faithfulness get retroactively reinterpreted as exploitation.

chronic.name: The Ledger
chronic.body: Every act of service becomes an entry someone owes. The Servant keeps the books privately and perfectly, and no one else knows they are in debt — which means no one can ever pay.

servant.needs: To be thanked for something specific rather than in general. To be asked rather than assumed. And explicit permission to stop.
servant.sayThis: I saw what you did, and I know what it cost you. What can I take off your plate?
servant.notThis: You didn't have to do that.
servant.notThisWhy: It is meant as absolution and lands as erasure. The Servant already paid the cost; being told it was unnecessary makes the payment meaningless rather than making it lighter.
servant.ownMove: Say the tally out loud. Ask directly for the thing you have been silently keeping score of. A ledger only has power while it is private — spoken, it turns back into an ordinary request that someone can actually grant.
servant.restoredBody: Work offered freely rather than banked — the kind of steady, unglamorous competence that holds up everything else and asks for nothing but honesty in return.

erudite.trigger: Being rushed, or being simplified. The Erudite descends when they are pushed to conclude before they have grounds, or when their carefulness is treated as an obstacle rather than a contribution.

descent.tell: The answer arrives wrapped in so many conditions that it stops being an answer.
descent.body: The Erudite hedges, footnotes, and defers. They will not commit until the case is airtight, and the case is never quite airtight. What presents as rigor is increasingly self-protection: an unqualified statement is a statement that can be wrong.
descent.cost: The room stops asking. The most carefully considered perspective available goes unheard because it never arrives in a usable form, and the Erudite reads the silence as confirmation that no one values depth.

descent.tell: Accuracy becomes a weapon.
descent.body: Being right stops being a service and starts being a position. The Erudite catches errors precisely, at the moment they will cost the other person the most, and defends the correction as intellectual honesty. Rigidity sets in — the standard hardens into law, and grace becomes indistinguishable from sloppiness.
descent.cost: They win points and lose people. Each victory makes the next conversation more guarded, and the Erudite ends up with the last word and no one left in the argument.

descent.tell: The door closes, and the silence does the punishing.
descent.body: The Erudite withdraws behind the wall of being right and stops coming out. Absence becomes the discipline they administer to a world that would not slow down for them. Any attempt to reach them registers as intrusion, so the reaching stops, which proves the withdrawal was warranted.
descent.cost: A mind built to illuminate now only archives. The Erudite is unreachable, entirely certain, and completely alone with the truth.

chronic.name: The Citadel
chronic.body: Correctness becomes a place to live rather than a thing to offer. The walls are real, the defenses are excellent, and no one has been inside in years.

erudite.needs: Time before a decision, and space that is not read as rejection. To be asked for their depth rather than for the short version of it.
erudite.sayThis: I want your read on this. Take the time you need — just tell me when you'll have it.
erudite.notThis: Can you just give me the bottom line?
erudite.notThisWhy: It tells the Erudite that their entire process is overhead. They will either withhold the analysis or deliver it in a form designed to prove the process was necessary.
erudite.ownMove: Offer the partial answer before it is finished, and label it as partial. Being useful now beats being unassailable later, and a clearly-flagged provisional read costs you nothing in credibility.
erudite.restoredBody: Knowledge delivered at the speed a person can actually receive it — depth in service of someone else's understanding rather than in defense of your own.

enthusiast.trigger: Disconnection. The Enthusiast descends when the relational bond feels at risk — when a room goes cold, when a conflict has no visible resolution, or when they suspect they are valued for the energy they supply rather than for who they are.

descent.tell: The energy goes up and the substance goes down.
descent.body: The Enthusiast fills the silence, amplifies the story, and works the room harder. Every gap gets a joke in it. They are not being dishonest — they are managing an anxiety they may not have named, and the tool they reach for is the one they are best at.
descent.cost: The performance succeeds and the person disappears behind it. The Enthusiast becomes the most visible and least known person in the room, which deepens exactly the isolation driving the behavior.

descent.tell: The hard thing gets reframed until it no longer has to be faced.
descent.body: Charm turns into management. The Enthusiast redirects, softens, and finds the angle that makes the difficult conversation unnecessary — sometimes with a formula or a slogan standing in where a real solution belongs. Under enough pressure they will start assigning blame elsewhere, because the alternative is holding it.
descent.cost: Problems get postponed rather than solved, and the people around them stop trusting the reassurance. Warmth that consistently precedes avoidance eventually stops reading as warmth.

descent.tell: The exit, framed as freedom.
descent.body: The Enthusiast leaves — the job, the church, the friendship — often abruptly and often with a story about how constricting it had become. Underneath the story is a conviction they may never say out loud: that they were never actually wanted, only enjoyed, and that leaving first is cheaper than being left.
descent.cost: A gift built to bind people together produces a life of unfinished relationships, each ended just before it could be tested.

chronic.name: The Performance
chronic.body: The room always gets the show and never gets the person. The Enthusiast is universally liked, thoroughly enjoyed, and known by almost no one — including, increasingly, themselves.

enthusiast.needs: To be wanted for who they are rather than for what they bring. Evidence that the relationship survives a hard conversation.
enthusiast.sayThis: I'm not going anywhere. We can sit in this until it's actually resolved.
enthusiast.notThis: Can you be serious for once?
enthusiast.notThisWhy: It tells the Enthusiast that their gift is the problem. They will either perform harder to win back approval or quietly write the relationship off as one more place they don't fit.
enthusiast.ownMove: Stay in the room after the energy runs out. Let one conversation be flat, unresolved, and unlit — and notice that no one leaves. The proof you need cannot be generated by the performance; it can only be found on the other side of stopping it.
enthusiast.restoredBody: Hope offered out of substance rather than out of performance — the kind that holds up because the person offering it stayed for the hard part.

host.trigger: Being treated as a source rather than a person. The Host descends when what they provide is consumed without acknowledgment, when generosity gets taken for granted, or when they cannot see any fruit from what they gave.

descent.tell: Generosity develops conditions.
descent.body: The Host begins measuring — quietly, and with real precision — what goes out against what comes back. Gifts still get given, but they are now being weighed first. Prudence is the language used for it, and prudence is a genuine part of this gift, which is what makes the shift so hard to catch.
descent.cost: The freedom drains out of the giving while the giving continues. Recipients feel the change before anyone can name it, and the warmth that made the provision meaningful starts to cool.

descent.tell: The gift becomes a lever.
descent.body: Provision starts purchasing compliance. There are strings, and everyone can feel them even when no one names them — the trip, the tuition, the job, the check, each carrying an unstated expectation about behavior or loyalty. The Host would call this stewardship. The people receiving it call it something else, privately.
descent.cost: Every future gift becomes suspect. Genuine generosity can no longer be received as generosity, because no one can tell anymore which offers have a hook in them.

descent.tell: The hand closes, and stays closed.
descent.body: The Host shuts down the flow entirely — resources, hospitality, warmth, presence — and calls it wisdom. They hoard, isolate, and build a case for why no one deserved it anyway. The gift that was meant to circulate has become a vault with the owner locked inside it.
descent.cost: Abundance without any joy in it. The Host ends with everything they gathered and no one they gathered it for.

chronic.name: The Vault
chronic.body: A hand that was made to open has learned to stay shut. What remains is accumulation without circulation, and a growing conviction that generosity was always naïve.

host.needs: To see the fruit of what they gave. To be received as a person and not only as a resource.
host.sayThis: Here's what your investment actually made possible. And separately — how are you doing?
host.notThisWhy: It confirms that they are a mechanism rather than a member. Every request that arrives before a relationship does moves the Host one notch toward the vault.
host.ownMove: Give one thing with no expectation of return and tell no one you did it. The ledger loses its grip the moment you prove to yourself that you can operate without it.
host.restoredBody: An open hand that is not paying for anything — provision offered because it is good, not because it secures something.

strategist.trigger: Loss of control over the outcome. The Strategist descends when the plan is undermined, when commitments quietly go unmet, or when they are held responsible for a result they were not given the authority to secure.

descent.tell: The grip closes on the plan.
descent.body: Delegation either stops or becomes assignment without trust — tasks handed out with the outcome already specified and the judgment withheld. The Strategist starts driving themselves harder than anyone and expecting the same, and begins to read as cold to people who were used to being led rather than deployed.
descent.cost: Ownership evaporates. People execute instructions instead of pursuing goals, which produces exactly the mediocrity that made the Strategist tighten in the first place.

descent.tell: People become resources to be spent.
descent.body: The Strategist rolls over objections to protect the plan. Sarcasm replaces persuasion because persuasion takes time they no longer believe they have. Human costs get logged as acceptable losses, and the mission becomes the justification for how the mission is being pursued.
descent.cost: The best people stop arguing, then stop caring, then leave. The Strategist wins the objective and loses the team that could have held it.

descent.tell: Total self-reliance, experienced as strength.
descent.body: Trust is gone. The Strategist runs everything alone, keeps their own counsel, and treats the resulting isolation as evidence of superior capability rather than as a symptom. Suspicion becomes the default posture, and the drivenness often migrates into the body — work, stimulants, punishing routines, anything that keeps the engine loud enough to drown the rest out.
descent.cost: A gift built to carry people ends up carrying everything alone. The load is real, the competence is real, and no one is left to share either.

chronic.name: The Command
chronic.body: Relationship collapses into chain of command. Everyone knows their assignment and no one knows the Strategist, including the people who report to them every day.

strategist.needs: Genuine agreement on the plan, or an honest renegotiation of it. Not silent non-compliance, which is the one thing they cannot work with.
strategist.sayThis: I'm with you on the plan. Here's the one part I need to change, and here's why.
strategist.notThis: Let's just see how it goes.
strategist.notThisWhy: It reads as abandonment of the mission. The Strategist hears that no one else is holding the outcome, and takes the whole weight back onto themselves.
strategist.ownMove: Ask one person what they think before you decide — and let the answer actually move the plan. Not consultation as theater. A plan that no one was allowed to shape is a plan no one will carry when you are not watching.
strategist.restoredBody: Leadership that carries people rather than spends them — the long, patient discipline of getting somewhere with everyone still aboard.

lover.trigger: Rejection, or the suspicion of it. The Lover descends when acceptance feels conditional, when conflict goes unrepaired, or when they sense that their inner world is too much for the people around them.

descent.tell: The room gets smoothed, and the cost gets absorbed.
descent.body: The Lover agrees to things they do not agree with, apologizes for things that were not theirs, and takes the tension of the room into their own body so no one else has to hold it. Their own need goes unspoken because speaking it might introduce friction, and friction is the thing they are working hardest to prevent.
descent.cost: The peace is real and it is being purchased with the Lover's self. No one knows the price is being paid, so no one thinks to stop it.

descent.tell: The hurt starts leaking out sideways.
descent.body: Over-explaining. Testing for reassurance. Long accounts of what happened that are really a request to be told they are still wanted. The Lover has too much feeling and no direct channel for it, so it comes out as confusion, defensiveness, or a hurt that everyone senses and no one can locate.
descent.cost: The people around them respond to the symptom rather than the need — reassuring the surface while the actual question goes unasked and unanswered.

descent.tell: A quiet that is not peace.
descent.body: The Lover goes still and unreachable, having concluded something that feels less like a thought than a fact: that they were never really wanted, only tolerated. Bitterness and unforgiveness settle in underneath the quiet, and the door that stays closed is the same door they spent years holding open for everyone else.
descent.cost: The most relationally gifted person in the room becomes the least reachable. And because the shutdown is silent, it is frequently mistaken for being fine.

chronic.name: The Erasure
chronic.body: The self dissolves into everyone else's comfort. The Lover is present in the room and absent from it, endlessly accommodating and quietly waiting to be noticed by someone who has been given no reason to look.

lover.needs: Acceptance that does not have to be earned, and to be told directly — in words, not inference — that they are wanted.
lover.sayThis: I want you here. Not because of what you do for us. I want you.
lover.notThisWhy: It confirms the fear underneath everything: that their inner world is too much, and that feeling deeply is a defect rather than the gift itself.
lover.ownMove: Say the unsmoothed thing. Name one need with no apology attached to the front of it and no justification attached to the back. The relationships worth having will hold it, and you cannot find out which ones those are while you are protecting everyone from you.
lover.restoredBody: Mercy given out of fullness rather than out of fear — the kind that can stay present to someone else's pain because it is no longer trying to earn a place in the room.
